obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise
citation: Merchant agreements MID-1 and MID-2 (fictional contract term)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to card data or payment systems
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (contract term; fictional)
notify: Acquiring bank (Controller calls the acquirer's risk line, then confirms in writing)

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, version 10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (North America contact in Table 1.1), normally coordinated through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - card brand rule applied through the merchant agreement

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2 and Attachment A
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
notify: Visa, through the acquirer's upload tools

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the acquirer; the PFI must not have provided other services to the hotel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required by Visa (Visa may instead require an independent investigation, Section A.6)

obligation: Other card brands (Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
citation: Each brand's operating rules (for Mastercard, its Security Rules and Procedures on account data compromise events)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per the brand's rules; timing not verified here. Follow the acquirer's instructions and treat 24 hours as the working target

trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information of Florida residents. Includes name plus ID card, driver license, or passport number (ID scans), and name plus card number with any required security code (keyed card entries)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (unless delayed by law enforcement or waived under 501.171(4)(c))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with synopsis, count, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

trigger: Hotel decides, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, that the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if this path is used; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the hotel (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the hotel (PMS vendor, chatbot vendor, cloud or marketing vendors) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The hotel (IT Manager and General Manager); the hotel then gives the 501.171(3) and (4) notices

trigger: Affected guests who reside outside Florida (most guests are out-of-state visitors)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of affected guests

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3.3.4 (recommended)
notify: U.S. Secret Service Electronic Crimes Task Force (as named in the Visa document); FBI (IC3)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if extortion occurs. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the hotel is below the SBA size standard and lodging has no proposed sector criterion

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
